messages:
sam: Heads-up — started scheduled BMC/BIOS push to us-west-2 around 02:10 UTC. We're seeing ~4% of nodes come back with UEFI Secure Boot enabled by default, which the provisioner rejects. GPU pool size dropped ~12 GPUs and the provisioning queue spiked. Anyone seen this pattern in the last roll?

infra-bot: [alert] deployment: bmc-bios-usw2 finished (batch 48/92) — 18 failures, 6 secureboot toggles detected. See https://inframon.redwood/deploys/2478901234

lee: ugh. do we have a concise list of affected hosts? can we hotfix via OOB without reimage? :thinking:

anya: grabbing logs — bmc response shows the flag flip during postflash: `GET /bmc/uefi/secureboot -> enabled` after the fw apply. snippet:

```
# response from 10.3.22.45
{
  "secure_boot": "enabled",
  "bios_version": "3.2.1-rc2",
  "last_update": "2026-03-19T02:12:15Z"
}
```

most nodes still reachable via OOB but provisioner refuses because boot policy mismatches. list incoming in a sec.

julian: two parallel options: 1) mass-toggle secureboot off via ipmi/ipmitool/kvm (fast, lower risk) 2) rollback BIOS to 3.2.0 baseline (safer for future) but requires reboots/provisioning windows. which do we pick given capacity hit?

ops-oncall: i'm on it. starting runbook 'oob-disable-secboot' against the 18 hosts that reported toggles. will also open a small canary to verify we don't brick anything. ETA 15m.

sam: sound plan. heads-up on capacity: we lost ~3 nodes in the dedicated pool too, so customer-facing latency is rising. julian, can we auto-route new provision requests to eu-west fallback or to the burst pool?

julian: yes, adding a short routing rule: route provision jobs from usw2 to eu and to burst for 30m. doing now — should reduce queue but will increase egress/cost. FYI ~estimated extra cost $120/hr while routing for the next 1h.

lee: ops-oncall, if OOB-runbook fails for any host, we should fall back to reprovision with `force_secure_boot=false` image. also capture full serial logs.

ops-oncall: acknowledged. running ipmitool command now on first canary:

```
ipmitool -H 10.3.22.45 -U admin -P *** raw 0x36 0x01 0x00
# toggles secureboot off (vendor raw command)
```

infra-bot: [update] canary 10.3.22.45 toggled -> provisioner accepted, node rejoined GPU pool (1 GPU). queue length reduced by ~7 jobs.

anya: collecting serial logs from failed hosts; there's a recurring message right after POST: `UEFI: SecureBoot variable set by vendor fw` — looks like the new BIOS defaults changed behavior.

sam: we need two action items: roll forward fix (hot-OOB toggle) and rollback plan for the next batch. also policy: vendor builds need to be validated that they don't flip secure boot without explicit config.

julian: agreed. scheduling a soft-hold on next batches until vendor confirms build flags. i'll also add a gating script in the deploy pipeline to query `/bmc/uefi/secureboot` post-flash and abort batch if any enabled.

lee: please add an alert to paging if pool drop >5% during a deploy — we missed a silent degradation earlier.

ops-oncall: FYI did OOB toggles on 16/18 hosts successfully. 2 hosts failed OOB (serial hangs). they are out for reprovision; starting reprovision now. keeping the incident log updated.

sam: nice. can we get a short postmortem entry? include cost impact, nodes affected, root cause hypothesis (BIOS default flip), and mitigation (pipeline gate + rollback).

anya: filing a short incident note in postmortems/ — will link here once done. early numbers: provisioning queue peaked ~220 -> baseline ~35; added ~0.9 GPU-hours of burst; est incremental cost $96 for the spike plus 2 reprovisions.

julian: vendor contact pinged, they say this was an unintentional default in 3.2.1 where the 'SecureBootDefault' bit flips to 'enabled' for certain SKUs. asking for stamp fix.

sam: ok. thanks everyone. keep watch on the routing rule and reprovision progress. once vendor patch lands we'll coordinate a safer resume schedule.

infra-bot: [resolved] routing rule removed at 03:15 UTC. final node count restored. incident marked as mitigated.
